# Jubilees Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Adam and Eve in Eden; The Fall; The Law of Purification

---

**3:1** During the six days of the second week, the angels brought every creature before Adam as God had commanded — wild animals on day one, livestock on day two, birds on day three, every land creature on day four, every water creature on day five.

**3:2** Adam gave each one a name, and whatever name he spoke became that creature's name forever.

**3:3** After surveying all of them over five days, Adam still had no companion who matched him.

**3:4** So the LORD said to the angels: "It is not good for man to live alone. Let us make him a partner who fits him."

**3:5** The LORD our God put Adam into a deep sleep, and while he slept, God took one of his ribs — that rib was the source of the woman, drawn from his own body — and closed up the flesh. Then God shaped the woman from that rib.

**3:6** God woke Adam up. When he opened his eyes on the sixth day and saw what God had brought to him, he recognized her at once and said: "This one — this is bone from my bones, flesh from my flesh. She will be called Woman, because she was drawn out of Man."

**3:7** "That is why a man leaves his father and mother and bonds himself to his wife, and the two become one flesh."

**3:8** Adam was created in the first week; his wife from his rib, in the second week. For the first time then, he was intimate with her. And from this pattern a law was drawn: for a male birth, seven days of purification; for a female birth, fourteen days.

**3:9** After Adam had spent forty days in the place of his creation, the angels led him into the garden of Eden to work and tend it. His wife was not brought in until the eightieth day — only then did she enter the garden.

**3:10** Because of this, the law is written on the heavenly tablets for every woman who gives birth: if she has a boy, she is unclean for seven days — counting from the first week — and then remains in her blood of purification for thirty-three more days. She must not touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until those days are done.

**3:11** If she has a girl, she is unclean for two full weeks, and then spends sixty-six more days in purification — eighty days in total.

**3:12** When Eve had finished those eighty days, the angels brought her into the garden of Eden — for the garden is holier than all other land on earth, and every tree growing in it is holy.

**3:13** So the law was set: whether a woman gives birth to a boy or a girl, she must not touch anything sacred or enter the sanctuary until those days run out.

**3:14** This law and testimony was inscribed for Israel on the heavenly tablets to be kept forever.

**3:15** In the first week of the first jubilee, Adam and his wife lived and worked in the garden of Eden for seven years. The angels gave them tasks and taught them everything that farming requires.

**3:16** He worked the garden, naked, with no knowledge of his nakedness and no shame. He kept the birds and animals from ruining the garden, gathered the fruit, ate his fill, and stored the rest for himself and his wife.

**3:17** After exactly seven years — in the second month, on the seventeenth day — the serpent slithered up to the woman and said: "Did God really tell you that you must not eat from every tree in the garden?"

**3:18** She answered: "God told us to eat freely from the trees in the garden. But the tree in the center? He said: 'Don't eat from it. Don't even touch it, or you will die.'"

**3:19** The serpent said: "You won't die at all. God knows that the moment you eat from it, your eyes will open. You will become like God — you will know good and evil."

**3:20** The woman looked at the tree: it was beautiful, good for eating, and it promised wisdom. She took the fruit and ate it. She covered herself with fig leaves and gave some of the fruit to her husband. He ate it too.

**3:21** His eyes flew open. He realized he was naked.

**3:22** He grabbed some fig leaves, stitched them together into a covering, and hid himself.

**3:23** God cursed the serpent and was furious with it — and remains so forever. He was angry with the woman too. And he was angry with Adam for listening to his wife and eating what God had forbidden.

**3:24** God expelled them from the garden of Eden. From that day on, he stationed the angels with a flaming, spinning sword at the east side of the garden to guard the path to the tree of life.

**3:25** The day Adam walked out of the garden, he made an offering — frankincense, galbanum, stacte, and spices — burning them in the morning as the sun rose, from the very day he had covered himself in shame.

**3:26** On that same day, the mouths of all the animals — wild, domestic, bird, crawler, swimmer — were shut permanently. They could no longer speak. Until that moment, all creatures had been speaking to one another in a single shared language.

**3:27** Every creature was driven out of the garden, and each kind was scattered to the region created for it.

**3:28** Of all the creatures, only Adam was given the knowledge of how to cover his nakedness.

**3:29** That is why the heavenly tablets decree that all who know the law must cover themselves — unlike the Gentiles, who go uncovered without shame.

**3:30** On the first day of the fourth month, Adam and his wife left the land of Eden and settled in the land of Elda, the region of their origins.

**3:31** Adam named his wife Eve.

**3:32** They had no children until the first jubilee. After that, Adam was intimate with her.

---
*PNEUMA notes: "Flaming, spinning sword" (v.24) draws on the Hebrew reckoning behind the Ge'ez; "cherubim" implied but not named here. The pre-fall animal speech (v.26) is a striking Jubilees-unique tradition — rendered directly. "Eightieth day" purification law rooted in Lev 12 is Jubilees' hermeneutical move.*
